kizunaNote: PostgREST RPC body for kizunasync.pull: top-level keys are SQL argument names. Client identity rides the optional client_id key (D-client-identity), with the Supabase Auth JWT session_id claim as the fallback when it is absent.

items.kizunaNote: A bucket is {table, params}. Current transcripts use one owner-equality bucket {"table":"todos","params":{"owner_id":"<user uuid>"}}; that fixture choice does not narrow the schema.

params.kizunaNote: Owner/tenant equality over indexed top-level columns (P:mutations-and-column-masked-conflict-resolution Bucket).

buckets.kizunaNote: Declared parameterized subsets (normative concept, P:mutations-and-column-masked-conflict-resolution Bucket). Live row images are RLS-scoped; tombstone identifiers are selected by the bucket, not by replaying RLS on a gone row. At most 64 entries: the SQL pack and the reference oracle refuse a longer list with SQLSTATE 22023 before any gate runs (D-page-cap-and-checkpoint-boundary). The SQL pack casts the bucket column's value through the column type once, so a pull of a bucketed table reads only the changelog entries labeled with a requested value (D-bucket-move-out).

client_id.kizunaNote: Optional client identity, decided by D-client-identity: when present the server registers the client under it, when absent it falls back to the Supabase Auth JWT session_id claim. A uuid string; the UUID placeholder grammar uses kind code c1.

cursor.kizunaNote: '0' = bootstrap. D-cursor-opaque-token selected an opaque text token: a decimal high-water mark, optionally followed by '~' and ascending dot-separated holes.

limit.kizunaNote: Optional; default 500. D-page-cap-and-checkpoint-boundary selected the name limit, which the public RPC uses, and selected has_more. Rows and tombstones count against the same cap, a page is a prefix of the (seq, table, pk) stream, and a page that holds every remaining entry closes the checkpoint. A page also stops once the server has examined its scan cap of candidates (_settings.max_pull_scan, default 5000), so a continuation page can hold fewer than limit entries. Integer >= 1.
